text:
lydia (Acme Corp): Hey team — after we moved to the private VPC deploy, our app started getting intermittent failures talking to our KMS proxy. Error in logs: "failed to fetch key: connection timeout". Happening ~20% of requests. Can you help?

lydia (Acme Corp): Relevant bits: private-redwood endpoint in our VPC, KMS endpoint is kms-internal.acme.svc.cluster.local -> 10.2.4.12. We see TLS handshake errors too: "alert handshake failure" in app logs.

sanjay (Support): Sorry for the trouble. Two quick Qs: 1) Are you using our KMS/HSM direct integration (TLS to customer KMS) or our passthrough proxy? 2) Any recent firewall/egress changes?

lydia (Acme Corp): We're using direct integration to our HSM (Thales) behind customer-controlled NAT. No intentional egress changes but infra team did a security group cleanup last week.

tim (Eng Infra): Copying troubleshooting steps from infra checklist. Can you run these from a host inside the same subnet as the Redwood connector?
1) dig kms-internal.acme.svc.cluster.local\2) curl -v https://kms-internal.acme.svc.cluster.local:443/health || true\3) openssl s_client -connect kms-internal.acme.svc.cluster.local:443 -servername kms-internal.acme.acme (show cert chain)

lydia (Acme Corp): Running them now, paste outputs:

--- dig ---
; <<>> DiG 9.11.3 <<>> kms-internal.acme.svc.cluster.local
;; ->>HEADER<<- opcode: QUERY, status: NOERROR, id: 12345
;; ANSWER SECTION:
kms-internal.acme.svc.cluster.local. 30 IN A 10.2.4.12

--- curl ---
* About to connect() to kms-internal.acme.svc.cluster.local port 443 (#0)
*   Trying 10.2.4.12...
* Connected to kms-internal.acme.svc.cluster.local (10.2.4.12) port 443 (#0)
* TLS 1.2 connection using TLSv1.2 / ECDHE-RSA-AES256-GCM-SHA384
* Server certificate: CN=kms.acme.internal
* SSL: certificate subject name (kms.acme.internal) does not match target host name 'kms-internal.acme.svc.cluster.local'
* Closing connection 0
curl: (51) SSL: certificate subject name (kms.acme.internal) does not match target host name 'kms-internal.acme.svc.cluster.local'

--- openssl s_client ---
CONNECTED(00000003)
depth=2 C = US, O = ExampleCA, CN = Example Root CA
verify error:num=20:unable to get local issuer certificate
verify return:1
depth=1 C = US, O = ExampleCA, CN = Inter CA
verify return:1
depth=0 CN = kms.acme.internal
verify return:1
---
Certificate chain
 0 s:/CN=kms.acme.internal
   i:/C=US/O=ExampleCA/CN=Inter CA
---

lydia (Acme Corp): So mismatch between cert CN and DNS name. We thought the device would have cert SANs but it's the appliance default CN.

maya (Eng ML): That CN mismatch would explain the SSL alerts. Redwood client validates SNI/hostname by default. Two paths: 1) update the HSM cert to include SAN for kms-internal.acme.svc.cluster.local, or 2) configure Redwood connector to use custom server_name override (SNI) and to skip host name verification for this endpoint if customer forces it (less ideal).

sanjay (Support): Agreed. Also check customer NAT/load-balancer SNI passthrough — if LB terminates TLS and reissues a certificate with CN that doesn't match, app will fail. Can you show the TLS termination point?

lydia (Acme Corp): Our infra team says TLS is terminated on the HSM appliance (no LB). They forwarded logs showing occasional "handshake failure (no shared cipher)" from HSM at same times. Could that be a cipher mismatch?

tim (Eng Infra): Yes — we should check cipher suites + TLS versions. Redwood runtime negotiates modern ciphers (TLS1.2+ ECDHE). Some older HSMs only support RSA key exchange or limited suites. Can you run:

openssl s_client -connect 10.2.4.12:443 -cipher 'ALL' -servername kms.acme.internal
and also with limiting to TLS1.2: 
openssl s_client -connect 10.2.4.12:443 -tls1_2 -cipher 'ECDHE' -servername kms.acme.internal

lydia (Acme Corp): Ran both. With -cipher ALL it connects but with -tls1_2 and ECDHE it fails. So the HSM only supports RSA key exchange and older suites.

maya (Eng ML): That explains intermittent timeouts: newer clients prefer ECDHE; when negotiation fails some connections fallback but others time out. We can do two things from Redwood side: rotate our connector to allow the legacy cipher for that specific endpoint, or insert a small TLS-negotiation proxy (stunnel) that speaks modern ciphers to Redwood and legacy to HSM.

sanjay (Support): For the short term you can add a connector-level override. Please note security implications (RSA key-exchange lacks forward secrecy). We'll need a signed change. Do you want us to open an infra change request with ops to add the override?

lydia (Acme Corp): Yes please. Also, separately, there are still timeouts even after we allowed legacy ciphers in a test — we still see ~5% failures with "connection reset by peer". Any firewall suggestions?

tim (Eng Infra): Check connection tracking timeouts and ephemeral port exhaustion on the HSM side. Also double-check security groups and NACLs allow established connections back to the connector's ephemeral ports. From the connector host run:

sudo ss -nt state established sport = :443
sudo conntrack -L | grep 10.2.4.12 || true

And verify the customer's NAT is not reusing source ports in a way that the HSM rejects sessions.

lydia (Acme Corp): We found that the NAT device has aggressive idle timeout of 30s. Increasing it to 300s reduced resets a lot.

oliver (Customer Success): Good catch — I've documented that in the runbook for private deployments: ensure NAT timeouts > 300s for long-lived KMS sessions.

sanjay (Support): To summarize recommended steps (we'll also create a support ticket with the infra change):
- Ensure HSM cert includes SANs for the internal DNS name (recommended).
- If not possible, add SNI override or CN verification exception on the connector (temporary).
- Allow legacy ciphers on connector only if HSM cannot be upgraded, and log+review risk.
- Raise NAT idle timeouts and confirm conntrack on HSM side.
- Ensure egress allowlist includes connector IPs and that ports 443/8443 are open.
- If still flaky, deploy an stunnel/tlsbridge in the customer VPC as a stable shim.

deploy-bot: Support ticket 34218 created (priority: high) assigned to eng-infra for connector TLS exceptions and to customer for HSM cert rotation.

lydia (Acme Corp): Thanks — we'll get the cert team to add SANs and will follow up once rotated. For now we'll accept the connector override while cert is rotated. Appreciate the quick triage.

sanjay (Support): Cool — keep us posted. Once cert is rotated we should revert connector overrides. I'll add rollback steps in the ticket.

maya (Eng ML): If you want, I can draft a short howto for customers that includes example stunnel config and recommended OpenSSL checks. Useful for future private customers with legacy HSMs.

lydia (Acme Corp): Please do. That would help our infra team.

oliver (Customer Success): Following up: added a KB entry to the private deploy runbook titled "KMS/HSM connectivity checklist" with items from above and a sample OpenSSL command list.

sanjay (Support): Closing note: if you see any TLS alerts in our logs referencing SNI mismatch or verify failed, tag them here and we'll prioritize.

lydia (Acme Corp): Will do. Closing the loop once cert rotation is done. Thanks everyone!
